subject: Renewal: Dedicated GPU top-up + burst contingency playbook
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: OrangeCloud Ops <ops@orangecloud.ai>, procurement@orangecloud.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: Dedicated GPU top-up + burst contingency playbook

Hi Maria / OrangeCloud team —

Following our renewal kickoff call, attached is a pragmatic proposal that combines a reserved pool top-up with a measured burst contingency for peak events. High-level summary: 

- Add 40x reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (3-year term or option for 12-month renewal).
- Throughput target: guaranteed baseline of 30k tokens/sec aggregate, 95th pct latency SLOs in the contract.
- Burst contingency: On-demand spillover enabled up to an additional 80 GPUs during spikes, billed at on-demand rate, with a monthly spend cap set at 25% over the committed monthly burn.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to quantized model variants when latency is trending up; customer-controlled hard cap option available (if you prefer no on-demand spillover).

Attachments: redwood_capacity_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal + cost table), capacity_workbook_ORC.xlsx (workbook with sizing scenarios).

Please review the workbook rows highlighted in orange — they show the two options we discussed: (A) conservative top-up + soft on-demand with cap, (B) larger commitment with a lower on-demand allowance and deeper discount.

Next steps: please confirm which burst policy you prefer by EOD Friday so we can lock pricing and generate an amendment for procurement. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Ortega <ops@orangecloud.ai>

Cc: procurement@orangecloud.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated GPU top-up + burst contingency playbook

Thanks Jonas — quick clarifying Qs from our side: 

1) That monthly spend cap on on-demand — is it a hard cap (rejecting traffic) or a billing-only cap (we keep running but you invoice us)?
2) If we pick the hard cap option, how does Redwood behave operationally when we hit it? Do you drop requests, queue, or route to smaller models?
3) Can we get short-term burst credits for first 60 days post-upgrade to smooth adoption?

We'll also need the SOC2 snapshot and your standard data residency clause for our security/compliance team — procurement will loop in legal once we pick the policy.

-Maria
Head of Platform Ops
OrangeCloud

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Ortega <ops@orangecloud.ai>, procurement@orangecloud.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated GPU top-up + burst contingency playbook

Maria — great questions. Answers inline: 

1) Spend cap behavior: by default the cap we propose is billing-only — traffic continues to route on-demand and you are invoiced up to the cap. We can offer an optional hard cap where Redwood will stop routing new on-demand requests once the cap is reached. The difference is operational: billing-only preserves availability at the expense of extra spend; hard cap preserves cost predictability at the expense of potential service degradation.

2) Hard cap behavior: when reached, new requests are queued for up to 5s and then routed to the fallback model (quantized, lower cost variant) if queueing cannot be served. We never drop requests silently — we always return an error or fallback response. This is implemented as an ordered policy: reserved capacity -> on-demand -> queued window -> fallback model -> 429 with reason header if configured to surface.

3) Burst credits: yes — we can provide 2 months of burst credit for the first 60 days (covers on-demand usage up to a pre-agreed threshold). We usually bill the net overage beyond that threshold. I'll put the exact numbers in the amendment.

Cc'ing Mina (Infra) and Aditya (Solutions) to confirm throughput SLO wording and any ops constraints for enabling queued windows.

Thanks,
Jonas
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Maria Ortega <ops@orangecloud.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated GPU top-up + burst contingency playbook

Maria / Jonas — technical notes from infra: 

- We can guarantee the baseline throughput (30k tokens/sec) from the reserved pool with the proposed topology. We'll include a troubleshooting runbook for double-checking KV-cache priming and warm pools.
- For on-demand spillover we recommend enabling automatic model-variant routing rather than immediate hard cap. Quantized variants reduce compute by ~2.5x and are a safer user experience.
- Queueing: 5s queue window is feasible, but we suggest 3-tier queueing: 1s local retry, 4s shared queue, then fallback. This prevents long tail latency and keeps error rates low.
- Implementation note: to support the monthly spend cap as billing-only while preserving availability we need a signed amendment that gives ops permission to enable on-demand across your reserved region and an SRE contact for emergency throttles.

I'll attach a short ops checklist in the Drive link for your SREs.

—Mina
Director, Inference Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: procurement@orangecloud.ai <procurement@orangecloud.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated GPU top-up + burst contingency playbook

Hi team — procurement and legal have reviewed both options. We propose the following: 

- Proceed with Option A (40x reserved GPUs) + on-demand spillover enabled as billing-only with a hard monthly billing cap set at 20% above committed spend.
- Redwood will provide two months of burst credits covering up to 50% of average peak in the workbook for onboarding.
- Include the queue + fallback model behavior Mina described in the amendment language.
- Add a 30-day SLA credit window for sustained breach of the throughput SLO (95th pct latency target), defined in the amendment.

Please issue an amendment (OD-78942-A) reflecting the above and include the SOC2 snapshot. We'll route internally for signature once we get the amendment.

Thanks,
Carla R.
Procurement Manager
OrangeCloud
